title: Accounts Receivable Aging Report: What It Is and How to Use It
summary: What an accounts receivable aging report is, how to read one, an example with the standard aging buckets, what it tells you, and how AI agents act on it.
body_markdown:
Not all unpaid invoices are equal. An invoice two days past due is routine; one ninety days past due is a problem. The **accounts receivable aging report** is the tool that makes that distinction visible, grouping every unpaid invoice by how long it has been outstanding so finance can see where the risk is, prioritize collections, and estimate how much of the receivables balance may never be collected.


This guide explains what an AR aging report is, how to read one, an example, what it tells you, and how AI agents act on it.


## **What is an accounts receivable aging report?**


An accounts receivable aging report (or AR aging report) is a summary of a company's unpaid customer invoices, organized by how long they have been outstanding, typically in buckets such as current, 1–30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, and 90+ days past due. It is usually broken down by customer, so you can see who owes what and how overdue it is. It is one of the most-used reports in accounts receivable and a standard output of any accounting system.


> The aging report is a heat map of your receivables: the further right a balance sits, the hotter the risk. It turns a single AR number into a prioritized action list.


## **How to read an AR aging report**


A typical aging report lists each customer across the aging buckets. An example:


Customer Current 1-30 31-60 61-90 90+ Total


Acme Corp $12,000 $4,000 $0 $0 $0 $16,000


Globex $0 $8,000 $5,000 $0 $0 $13,000


Initech $0 $0 $0 $2,000 $7,500 $9,500


Total $12,000 $12,000 $5,000 $2,000 $7,500 $38,500


Reading across: Acme is healthy (mostly current), Globex is slipping (balances in the 1–60 buckets), and Initech is a red flag ($9,500 that is 61+ days past due, including $7,500 over 90 days). The columns on the right are where collections effort and credit concern should concentrate.


## **What the aging report tells you**


- **Collections priorities.** Which overdue accounts to chase first, usually the largest and most overdue.
- **Credit risk.** Customers who consistently drift into the late buckets may need tighter credit terms.
- **Bad-debt estimates.** The aging is the basis for the[allowance for doubtful accounts](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/allowance-for-doubtful-accounts) , since older balances are less likely to be collected.
- **DSO context.** The aging profile helps explain movements in[days sales outstanding](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/days-sales-outstanding) .


## **The limitation of a static aging report**


An aging report is a snapshot, and on its own it only tells you where things stand, not what to do or get it done. In most teams, someone exports the aging, decides who to chase, and then manually drafts and sends follow-ups, every week. By the next report, the picture has already changed. The value is in acting on the aging quickly and consistently, which is exactly where it tends to break down.


## **How AI agents act on the aging report**


AI agents turn the aging report from a static snapshot into an action engine. An agent can monitor the aging continuously, prioritize accounts by size and risk, draft and send collections follow-ups, log responses, and keep the aging current, so overdue invoices get worked the moment they slip rather than at the next manual review. The AR team supervises and owns the customer relationships while the agent does the chasing.

## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is an accounts receivable aging report?**


An AR aging report summarizes unpaid customer invoices grouped by how long they have been outstanding, typically in buckets like current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90, and 90+ days, usually broken down by customer. It shows who owes what and how overdue, to guide collections and gauge credit risk.


### **How do you read an AR aging report?**


Read across each customer's row through the aging buckets. Balances in the current and 1–30 columns are healthy; balances drifting into 61–90 and 90+ are collection and credit risks. Concentrate collections effort on the largest, most overdue balances on the right.


### **What are the standard AR aging buckets?**


The standard buckets are current (not yet due), 1–30 days past due, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, and 90+ days past due. Some teams use 30-day bands out to 120+ days. Older buckets indicate higher risk that the balance will not be collected.


### **How is the aging report used for bad debt?**


The aging report is the basis for estimating the allowance for doubtful accounts: companies apply higher uncollectible percentages to older buckets, since balances past 90 days are far less likely to be collected, to estimate how much of AR may never be received.


## **The bottom line**


The accounts receivable aging report groups unpaid invoices by how overdue they are, turning a single AR balance into a prioritized view of collections and credit risk. Reading it is straightforward; acting on it consistently is the hard part. The clearest shift in 2026 is AI agents that monitor the aging continuously and run collections on it, so overdue invoices get worked in real time.
